text:
Alyssa Rivera: paging SRE — we're seeing a spike of worker restarts and NCCL errors on tensor-parallel jobs in gpu-pool-3. Customers in us-west1 reporting degraded throughput.
incident-bot: Incident Pager (SEV2) — Serving runtime: multi-GPU collective failures detected. Notifying @oncall-sre. Auto-triage: pod-restarts > 5 in 10m, netlink flaps observed.
Carlos Nguyen: I'm taking lead. Starting with node health and kernel logs. Maya, can you pull customer-facing impact?
Maya Patel: CS has one enterprise customer (acme-inc) with 2 model-serving sessions failing with 503 / streaming cutouts. They're seeing ~20% error rate. I'll notify them we're investigating and will follow up in 30m.
Samir Rao: Quick notes from the runtime metrics: NCCL ERRORs aligned with container restarts ~1765432088-1765432150. GPU temps normal, but dmesg shows repeated PCIe link resets on node gpu-node-17.
Carlos Nguyen: Running kubectl describe on the affected pod:\n```\nkubectl -n inference describe pod tp-infer-62\nEvents:\n  Warning  Unhealthy  2m (x12 over 9m)  kubelet  Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503\n  Normal   Killing    1m (x4 over 3m)   kubelet  Killing container with id docker://runtime: Container failed liveness probe\n```\nAlyssa Rivera: Any OOM logs?
Samir Rao: No obvious oom_kill in dmesg. But docker logs show repeated NCCL communicator resets: \n```\n[2026-05-17 14:01:22] NCCL WARN Group 0 rank 1 errno 116 (Protocol error)\n[2026-05-17 14:01:23] NCCL INFO communicator reset triggered for comm id 0x7f2b3c\n[2026-05-17 14:01:24] runtime: failed to init net transport, fallback enabled\n```\nCarlos Nguyen: Looks like a link-level reset between ranks. Could be node-level flapping—either NIC/ib or the VM losing PCIe connectivity. Next steps: cordon gpu-node-17, drain non-critical pods, and restart the runtime container on the remaining nodes to re-establish stable communicators.
Alyssa Rivera: Agreed. Samir, can you trigger a drain on gpu-node-17 and set pod disruption budget overrides?
Samir Rao: Doing drain now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Samir Rao: Drain started. A few lower-priority workloads will be rescheduled. Notifying autoscaler to avoid immediate reprovision while we stabilize.
Maya Patel: CS update posted to customer: "We're investigating a multi-GPU network fault impacting inference in us-west1. We've isolated the node and are mitigating; will update in 30 minutes."
incident-bot: Automated check: no degraded storage, control plane healthy, node gpu-node-17 shows NIC link flaps recorded by cloud provider at 14:02:10-14:05:00.
Carlos Nguyen: After drain, I restarted runtime on affected TP pods with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/tp-runtime`. Watching logs for NCCL reconvergence.
Samir Rao: Post-drain logs: single occurrences of NCCL WARN during failover but then successful negotiates.\n```\n[2026-05-17 14:07:10] NCCL INFO Rank 0 connected to Rank 1\n[2026-05-17 14:07:12] NCCL INFO Allreduce done, latency within baseline\n```\nAlyssa Rivera: Did we restore customer sessions? Maya?
Maya Patel: Customer reported sessions recovered at 14:08. Error rate back to baseline ~0.5%. I confirmed with CS slack thread.
Carlos Nguyen: Root cause hypothesis: transient PCIe/NIC flaps on gpu-node-17 induced NCCL communicator resets. The runtime didn't gracefully degrade because the tensor-parallel launcher expected persistent ranks and encountered early communicator failure, causing liveness checks to fail and the orchestrator to kill containers.
Samir Rao: Immediate mitigations taken: 1) cordoned and drained gpu-node-17, 2) restarted tp-runtime pods to re-form NCCL communicators, 3) prevented autoscaler churn for 10m.
Alyssa Rivera: Longer term action items: create a health-check gating for NCCL errors to delay liveness kills until communicator reconverges (configurable timeout), and add node NIC flapping alerts to oncall. Also run an automated test simulating NIC resets to validate runtime recovery.
Maya Patel: I'll open the customer RCA draft and schedule a follow-up with ACME.
Carlos Nguyen: For the postmortem: collect `dmesg`, `docker logs`, `kubectl events`, and cloud-provider network event timeline for gpu-node-17. Tag logs with trace ids for the affected requests.
incident-bot: Handoff reminder — @oncall-sre please acknowledge. If you need to escalate to infra networking, ping @networking-team.
oncall-sre: Acknowledged. I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with networking. Adding action items to tracking ticket INF-4123.
Alyssa Rivera: Thanks all. Keeping this SEV2 open until postmortem and mitigation rollout planned. Closing the page when RCA and mitigation PR in place. :white_check_mark:
CS Bot: Customer message sent to acme-inc at 14:10 with ETA for detailed follow-up.
Carlos Nguyen: Final note — recommend a temporary increase to NCCL timeout in runtime config for tensor-parallel jobs while we tune; will draft PR.
Samir Rao: Adding logs to the incident bundle now.
Maya Patel: I'll post a short status update in 30m and then again after RCA."
